text:
Alice H: quick heads up — hit a nasty duplicate-side-effect issue when replaying streaming requests after a 429 + dropped socket.
Ben T: ugh. can you summarize reproduction steps?
Alice H: yep. flow: client starts streaming -> server emits partial event (and triggers downstream DB write via webhook) -> network hiccup -> SDK retries (429/short backoff) -> server receives replay and does second webhook write.
Cara M: so the SDK treats the stream as "retryable" since connection closed with 429?
Alice H: exactly. Node SDK currently retries the whole request if it gets 429 or a connection reset; no stream-resume token. Python client has an opt-in `safe_replay` shim but it only works for non-streaming endpoints.
Emma R: are we seeing this in production or only in a sample app?
Alice H: both. Saw it first in local sample (sample-app/streaming-checker) then a customer hit it in beta.
Frank L: screencap? logs?
Alice H: pasted minimal repro below — streaming endpoint that emits event {id, phase} then calls webhook. If the socket drops after phase==1, server already called webhook. SDK retries and we double-insert.
Ben T: can the server idempotent-key the webhook with event.id? that’s a server safety net.
Alice H: yes but customer can't change third-party webhook. We need client-side mitigations.
Cara M: brainstorm: 1) idempotency token header for whole request (but streaming chunks may represent multiple logical events) 2) stream-resume token — server issues token on first chunk that is persisted so replayed request can supply resume token and server rejects duplicate on resume window 3) client-side "replay-guard" that refuses to retry streaming requests unless `allow_unsafe_replay=true`.
Emma R: interesting. Which options are feasible for SDK parity? Node + Python + Go should have same behavior.
Frank L: I sketched a middleware:
```js
// pseudo: replay-guard middleware for Node SDK
client.use(async (req, next) => {
  if (req.stream) {
    // attach local replay fingerprint
    req.headers['x-rw-replay-fp'] = hash([req.path, req.body?.prompt?.slice(0,64), req.idempotency_key]);
    // only retry on idempotent-safe status codes
    const res = await next();
    if (res.status === 429 || res.status >= 500) {
      // check server resume support header
      if (!res.headers['x-rw-resume-token']) throw new RetryBlocked('streaming no-resume');
    }
    return res;
  }
  return next();
});
```
Ben T: love it. two notes: 1) hashing prompt prefixes can leak PII if we log it — make sure it's salted. 2) what about `Connection: keep-alive` churns?
Alice H: good catch — we should salt with a client secret and only store ephemeral fingerprint in memory. Also we should document: if `x-rw-resume-token` absent, SDK will NOT auto-retry streaming requests.
DeployBot: new deploy queued for branch feat/replay-guard (CI #4128) :rocket:
Cara M: sample-app updated in `examples/streaming-replay-guard` — uses a fake webhook and demonstrates the double-write. I added a toggle `REPLAY_GUARD=1`.
Emma R: SDK parity plan? Ideally: Node default to safe, Python add matching `safe_stream_replay=true` flag, Go mirror behavior.
Frank L: I filed a tiny API change request: server to include header `x-rw-resume-token` on the first flush and accept `x-rw-resume-token` on retries. That lets us keep behavior explicit.
Alice H: attaching short repro steps:
1) run `./examples/streaming-replay-guard/server`
2) run `./examples/streaming-replay-guard/client --drop-after=1`
3) observe webhook called twice when `REPLAY_GUARD=0`, single call when `REPLAY_GUARD=1`

Logs snippet:```
server: received chunk phase=1 id=abc123
server: webhook POST /notify id=abc123 -> 200
client: connection reset by peer
sdk: retrying request (stream) -> no x-rw-resume-token, replaying whole stream
server: received chunk phase=1 id=abc123 (duplicate)
server: webhook POST /notify id=abc123 -> 200 (duplicate)
```
Ben T: should we also add a small e2e test to the SDKs? a CI job that flips `REPLAY_GUARD` off and on to assert behavior.
Cara M: yep done in Node repo; adding Python PR now.
Emma R: docs note: call out that `idempotency_key` alone does NOT protect streaming endpoints. Add example code for using resume tokens and the guard.
Frank L: for telemetry, emit metric `sdk.replay_blocked` and `sdk.resume_token_seen` so we can measure how many customers rely on this.
Alice H: ok action items: Ben — review middleware salt approach; Cara — python PR + sample app; Frank — server header change RFC; Emma — docs patch; I'll open a short RFC issue linking samples and test vectors.
Ben T: 👍 will do review today.
Alice H: thanks all. cc @everyone if you want to test the sample app: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/tree/main/streaming-replay-guard :eyes:
